Wick Avenue & YSU 13

  1. Must see · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Butler Institute of American Art

    Opened in 1919 as the first museum in the country built solely for American art, with more than 20,000 works from Winslow Homer to the present. Free, and the anchor of the Wick Avenue museum row — the piece of Youngstown that draws visitors from out of state.

    Look for Free. Open Tuesday–Sunday. Approximate map pin.

    524 Wick Ave

    Recommended by Travel2Next, Ohio tourism, Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB)

  2. Must see · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Youngstown Historical Center of Industry and Labor

    The Steel Museum — an Ohio History Connection site that tells the rise and collapse of the mills that built Youngstown, straight and unsentimental. The essential stop for understanding what this city was and what happened to it.

    Your guide’s note Admission charged. Check open days; often Wed–Sat.

    151 W Wood St

    Recommended by Ohio tourism, Travel2Next

  3. Must see · Deli & Sandwiches · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Kravitz Delicatessen

    A classic Jewish delicatessen north of downtown, widely called the best corned beef in the Valley — plus rye, latkes and the rest of the deli canon.

    Your guide’s note Lunch counter; go for the corned beef. Approximate pin.

    3135 Belmont Ave, Liberty

    Recommended by HometownPlate

  4. Worth the detour · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Rose Melnick Medical Museum

    YSU's history-of-medicine museum: office recreations, nursing and x-ray exhibits, and a bright yellow 1952 Emerson iron lung as its centrepiece. Founded 1985; now in Cushwa Hall. An Atlas Obscura listing.

    Your guide’s note Free. Campus building — check hours; parking is easier on weekends.

    Cushwa Hall, Youngstown State University

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Youngstown State University

  5. Worth the detour · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Ward Beecher Planetarium

    A well-regarded university planetarium that has run free public shows since 1967 — typically Friday and Saturday evenings and Saturday afternoons, September through May.

    Your guide’s note Free, no reservations. Doors 30 min early; latecomers cannot enter once dark. Shows Sept–May.

    Ward Beecher Science Hall, 100 Lincoln Ave

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB), Youngstown State University

  6. Worth the detour · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Arms Family Museum

    A 1905 Arts-and-Crafts mansion run by the Mahoning Valley Historical Society, furnished as it was and used to tell the story of the Valley's industrial families.

    Your guide’s note Admission charged. Closed Mondays; check seasonal hours.

    648 Wick Ave

    Recommended by Mahoning Valley Historical Society

  7. Worth the detour · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Stambaugh Auditorium

    A 1926 neoclassical concert hall with a marble-columned front, one of the finest rooms in the region and still a working venue, just north of Wick Park.

    Your guide’s note Ticketed events; the exterior is worth a look any time.

    1000 Fifth Ave

    Recommended by Travel2Next

  8. Worth the detour · Italian · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Golden Dawn

    A 1932 Brier Hill Italian-American landmark on Logan Avenue. It closed in 2017 and has since reopened — running again, tied to the neighbourhood's pizza lore.

    Your guide’s note Reopened after 2017; confirm current hours before going.

    1245 Logan Ave

    Recommended by The Business Journal

  9. Worth the detour · Markets · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Northside Farmers Market

    Youngstown's oldest farmers market, running since 2003 near Wick Park — a dozen-plus local growers with produce, preserves, plants and prepared food, and the occasional live music or demo. Small but excellent, and a genuine community institution.

    Your guide’s note Saturday mornings (about 10–1); seasonal, so check the schedule before going. Publicly open.

    901 Elm St, North Side

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning

  10. Deep cut · Wick Avenue & YSU

    McDonough Museum of Art

    Youngstown State's contemporary art museum, directly across Wick Avenue from the Butler. Rotating shows of new and student work. Free.

    Your guide’s note Free. Often closed between exhibitions — check the current show.

    525 Wick Ave

    Recommended by Added by the guide (general knowledge)

  11. Deep cut · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Clarence R. Smith Mineral Museum

    A quiet hidden gem for rock hounds inside YSU — fluorescent minerals, fossils and crystals, free to walk through. Small, specific, and exactly the kind of thing this guide is for.

    Your guide’s note Free. Campus building; limited hours — check before going.

    Moser Hall, Youngstown State University

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB)

  12. Deep cut · Wick Avenue & YSU

    Wick Park

    A 34-acre 19th-century park ringed by the North Side's grand old mansions. A stroll and some architecture, not a ticket.

    Look for Free, daylight hours. Nicer by day.

    Fifth Ave & Park Ave, North Side

    Recommended by Added by the guide (general knowledge)

  13. Deep cut · Brier Hill & Pizza · Wick Avenue & YSU

    St. Anthony of Padua parish pizza

    The Brier Hill church that sells hundreds of pizzas a week as a parish fundraiser — takeout, cash, and a genuine piece of neighbourhood lore.

    Your guide’s note Fundraiser hours only — call ahead. Cash. Approximate pin.

    Brier Hill

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning

Mill Creek Park & West Side 12

  1. Must see · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Lanterman's Mill

    An 1845–46 grist mill, restored and still grinding corn, wheat and buckwheat with the creek's rushing water, beside a waterfall. The picture-book heart of Mill Creek Park.

    Your guide’s note Seasonal — roughly May through October. Small admission. Approximate pin.

    1001 Canfield Rd, Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Mill Creek MetroParks, Travel2Next, Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB)

  2. Must see · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Fellows Riverside Gardens

    Free formal gardens overlooking Lake Glacier, with the Davis visitor center, a cafe and long seasonal colour. Part of Mill Creek MetroParks and one of the loveliest free things in the Valley.

    Your guide’s note Free. Gardens open daily; Davis Center has its own hours.

    123 McKinley Ave, Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Mill Creek MetroParks, Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB)

  3. Must see · Dessert · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Handel's Homemade Ice Cream

    Founded here in the summer of 1945 by Alice Handel at her husband's gas station; the original South Side stand still scoops. Now 175+ stores nationwide, with its HQ in Canfield.

    Your guide’s note Cash-friendly, seasonal lines. The original location marks Handel's roots.

    7485 South Ave, Boardman

    Recommended by Handel's official history

  4. Worth the detour · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Mill Creek Suspension Bridge (the Cinderella Bridge)

    The slender 86-foot pedestrian suspension span locals call the Cinderella Bridge, recently restored to its arches-and-spires opulence. The park's signature photo, and an Atlas Obscura listing.

    Your guide’s note Free, always open. Approximate pin — it sits on a park trail.

    Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Mill Creek MetroParks

  5. Worth the detour · Brier Hill & Pizza · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Wedgewood Pizza

    A local pizzeria since 1967 that makes the classic Brier Hill pie — tomato, bell peppers and grated romano, with little or no mozzarella.

    Your guide’s note In Austintown, west of the city. Ask for the Brier Hill pie by name.

    Austintown, OH

    Recommended by HometownPlate, Wikipedia

  6. Worth the detour · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Lily Pond

    A restored pond circled by the quarter-mile Lily Pond Circle Trail — a short, flat, genuinely peaceful loop, revived from years of neglect with bioswales and permeable paving.

    Your guide’s note Free. Easy quarter-mile loop; good with kids. Approximate pin.

    Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Mill Creek MetroParks

  7. Worth the detour · Markets · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    The Amish Market

    A permanent indoor Amish market on South Avenue: bulk foods, baked goods, produce, meats, cheese and dairy, plus Amish furniture and a hot-food restaurant, all under one roof. A genuine fixture, not a pop-up.

    Your guide’s note Thu 9–6, Fri 9–6, Sat 8–4; closed Sun–Wed. Cash-friendly. Approximate pin.

    6121 South Ave, Boardman

    Recommended by Youngstown Live (Mahoning County CVB)

  8. Deep cut · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Lake Newport & Newport Boathouse

    At 60 acres the largest of the park's three lakes. Kayaks and pedal boats rent from the Newport Boathouse in season — the easiest way to get out on the water in the city.

    Your guide’s note Boat rentals seasonal; the drive around the lakes is open year-round.

    Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Mill Creek MetroParks

  9. Deep cut · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Joanne Beeghly Rose Garden

    A formal rose garden within Fellows Riverside Gardens, growing many classes of roses — at its best in June and July.

    Your guide’s note Free, within the gardens. Peak bloom early summer.

    Fellows Riverside Gardens, Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Mill Creek MetroParks

  10. Deep cut · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Ford Nature Center

    A stone-house nature center and trailhead into the wooded interior of Mill Creek Park, with exhibits and easy walks.

    Your guide’s note Free. Check hours; trails open dawn to dusk.

    840 Old Furnace Rd, Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Mill Creek MetroParks

  11. Deep cut · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Pioneer Pavilion

    An 1821 stone woolen-mill building, one of the oldest structures around, remodeled in 1893 and now a rentable pavilion for reunions and receptions.

    Your guide’s note Free to look; rentable for events. Combine with Lanterman's Mill.

    Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Mill Creek MetroParks

  12. Deep cut · Mill Creek Park & West Side

    Mill Creek Golf Course

    Two 18-hole, par-70 championship courses that opened to the public in 1928, laid through the park's woods — a genuine draw for golfers.

    Your guide’s note Tee times through the MetroParks. Seasonal. Approximate pin.

    1 W Golf Dr, Mill Creek Park

    Recommended by Mill Creek MetroParks

Downtown 16

  1. Must see · Italian · Downtown

    Yosteria

    A downtown Italian spot that regularly tops the city's restaurant lists, praised for its ricotta board and made-to-order pastas.

    Your guide’s note Popular; reservations help on weekends. Approximate pin.

    downtown Youngstown

    Recommended by HometownPlate, Explore Mahoning

  2. Must see · Downtown

    DeYor Performing Arts Center (Powers Auditorium)

    Home of the Youngstown Symphony, behind a 1931 movie-palace facade on West Federal Street. The Valley's main stage for orchestra, ballet and touring shows.

    Your guide’s note Ticketed performances. Lobby worth a peek on show nights.

    260 W Federal St

    Recommended by Added by the guide (general knowledge)

  3. Must see · Italian · Downtown

    Cassese's MVR

    Open since 1927. The dish is a Brier Hill 'Smoky Hollow' pizza — tomato, bell peppers and grated romano — eaten beside the bocce courts out back. As Youngstown as it gets.

    Your guide’s note Italian institution; bocce in season. Confirm hours.

    410 N Walnut St

    Recommended by HometownPlate

  4. Must see · Markets · Downtown

    The Youngstown Flea

    Downtown's premier 'Market for Makers' — a monthly, tightly curated indoor/outdoor market of local artists, vintage sellers, antique and repurposed furniture, apparel and food that draws treasure-hunters from across the region. One of the best reasons to be downtown on a market day.

    Your guide’s note Monthly during its season — check youngstownflea.com for dates before going. Publicly open.

    365 E Boardman St (downtown)

    Recommended by The Youngstown Flea

  5. Worth the detour · Downtown

    Mahoning County Courthouse

    A 1910 Renaissance Revival landmark by Charles F. Owsley whose interior opens into a roughly 100-foot rotunda crowned by a glazed art-glass dome, ringed by marble columns, mahogany and courtroom murals.

    Your guide’s note Working courthouse; the interior is best seen on the periodic free public tours. Security screening applies. Approximate pin.

    120 Market St, Youngstown, OH

    Recommended by Mahoning Matters, The Business Journal, WFMJ 21

  6. Worth the detour · Drinks & Breweries · Downtown

    Noble Creature Wild Ales & Lagers

    A downtown microbrewery in a historic church, all beer made onsite, specialising in wild ales and lagers — a distinctive taproom.

    Your guide’s note Taproom hours vary; check before you go. Approximate pin.

    101 E Boardman St

    Recommended by HometownPlate, The Vindicator

  7. Worth the detour · Drinks & Breweries · Downtown

    Penguin City Brewing Company

    A downtown brewery in a former warehouse, pitched as Youngstown's go-to hometown beer, with a big room, a disco ball and live music. Named for the city's old 'Penguin' nickname.

    Your guide’s note Taproom; check hours and events. Approximate pin.

    460 E Federal St

    Recommended by The Business Journal, The Vindicator

  8. Worth the detour · Downtown

    Tyler History Center

    The Historical Society's downtown museum of Mahoning Valley history, in a restored former department store on West Federal Street.

    Your guide’s note Admission charged. Check open days before going.

    325 W Federal St

    Recommended by Mahoning Valley Historical Society

  9. Worth the detour · Downtown

    Roger & Gloria Jones Children's Center for Science & Technology

    A hands-on STEM center for kids that opened in 2011, with interactive science and technology exhibits — the family stop downtown.

    Your guide’s note Admission charged; best for children. Check hours. Approximate pin.

    Downtown Youngstown

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB)

  10. Worth the detour · Downtown

    The Youngstown Playhouse

    Among the oldest continuously operating community theaters in the United States, staging affordable productions on the South Side.

    Your guide’s note Tickets are cheap; check the season's schedule.

    600 Playhouse Ln

    Recommended by Travel2Next

  11. Worth the detour · Brier Hill & Pizza · Downtown

    Avalon Downtown Pizzeria

    A brick-walled downtown spot serving Brier Hill pizza alongside inventions like a Pesto Hot Honey pie.

    Look for Downtown; good lunch stop between museums.

    Downtown Youngstown

    Recommended by HometownPlate

  12. Worth the detour · American · Downtown

    The Federal

    A bar and gathering spot on Federal Plaza with a patio and frequent live music — the social heart of downtown after dark, with a solid American menu.

    Your guide’s note Bar/venue; check the music calendar. Approximate pin.

    101 W Federal St

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning

  13. Worth the detour · Cafe & Coffee · Downtown

    The Mocha House

    A long-running cafe known for towering cakes, pastries and coffee, with a comfortable downtown room for a slower stop.

    Your guide’s note Cafe hours; save room for cake. Approximate pin.

    downtown Youngstown

    Recommended by HometownPlate

  14. Deep cut · Downtown

    Covelli Centre

    The downtown riverfront arena — Phantoms hockey, concerts and events, and the anchor of the eastern edge of downtown.

    Your guide’s note Event venue; nothing to see when dark. Check the calendar.

    229 E Front St

    Recommended by Added by the guide (general knowledge)

  15. Deep cut · Downtown

    Downtown Youngstown murals

    A growing set of large downtown murals, several honoured statewide, that have brightened the old commercial core. Walkable in an afternoon between Central Square and the arts district.

    Your guide’s note Free, outdoors, always up. Ask at a downtown shop for the current mural map. Approximate pin.

    around W Federal St & Central Square

    Recommended by The Business Journal

  16. Deep cut · Italian · Downtown

    Casa Di Canzonetta

    A well-liked Italian restaurant that turns up alongside the city's best, for a sit-down red-sauce dinner.

    Look for Dinner; confirm hours. Approximate pin.

    downtown Youngstown

    Recommended by HometownPlate

Mahoning Valley Day Trips 21

  1. Must see · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Past Times Arcade

    A retro pinball-and-arcade museum in a former Girard supermarket holding roughly 600 largely playable pinball machines plus 200+ classic arcade games from the 1930s on — one of the largest such collections in the country, assembled by Pinball Expo founder Rob Berk.

    Your guide’s note Opened 2023. Thu–Fri from 4pm, Sat–Sun from 11am; ~$20 adults / $10 ages 6–16 for unlimited play; allow 3+ hours. ~10 min north, off I-80. Approximate pin.

    419 N State St, Girard, OH

    Recommended by WFMJ 21, The Business Journal, Mahoning Matters, Tribune Chronicle, RePlay Magazine, Tripadvisor, Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB)

  2. Must see · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    National Packard Museum

    A 23,000-sq-ft museum on the site where the Packard automobile was born in 1899 — rotating original and restored Packards, classic motorcycles, and the Packard family and company archives.

    Your guide’s note Tue–Sat 12–5, Sun 1–5; closed Mondays and holidays. In Warren, ~20 min north. Approximate pin.

    1899 Mahoning Ave NW, Warren, OH

    Recommended by Ohio tourism, Tripadvisor, Truly Trumbull (Trumbull County CVB)

  3. Must see · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Robins Theatre

    A meticulously restored 1923 Art Deco/Mediterranean theatre by C. Howard Crane — a 1,400-seat house that reopened in 2020, ninety-seven years to the day after its debut, and now books national touring music and comedy.

    Your guide’s note Ticketed events; check the schedule. In downtown Warren, ~20 min north. Approximate pin.

    160 E Market St, Warren, OH

    Recommended by WKBN 27, Truly Trumbull (Trumbull County CVB), Tripadvisor

  4. Must see · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Dave Grohl Alley

    A brick alley in downtown Warren painted wall-to-wall in tribute to Warren-born Nirvana/Foo Fighters drummer Dave Grohl — murals, a metal figure at a drum kit, and a pair of 900-pound drumsticks billed as the world's largest.

    Your guide’s note Free, outdoors. In Warren, about 20 minutes north; pair with a Modern Methods beer next door.

    125 David Grohl Alley, Warren, OH

    Recommended by Ohio Magazine, The Business Journal

  5. Must see · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    National McKinley Birthplace Memorial & Museum

    A columned memorial and museum to President William McKinley in his birthplace of Niles, a short drive north of Youngstown. Free, and grander than you expect for a small city.

    Your guide’s note Free. In Niles, about 15 minutes away. Check museum hours.

    40 N Main St, Niles, OH

    Recommended by Added by the guide (general knowledge)

  6. Worth the detour · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Mill Creek MetroParks Farm

    A 402-acre working farm run by Mill Creek MetroParks — animal barns, the interactive AgVenture Barn, a free fall corn maze, disc golf and a natural playground — and the trailhead for the 11-mile MetroParks Bikeway.

    Your guide’s note Seasonal, roughly April–October; free admission. Pumpkin harvest and Bug Day in season. ~20 min south. Approximate pin.

    7574 Columbiana-Canfield Rd, Canfield, OH

    Recommended by Ohio tourism, Mill Creek MetroParks, Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB)

  7. Worth the detour · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Noah's Lost Ark Exotic Animal Sanctuary

    A nonprofit no-kill exotic-animal sanctuary — lions, tigers, bears and 125+ rescued animals — one of the few facilities both state- and federally licensed to give guided public tours.

    Your guide’s note Seasonal, roughly May 15–Oct 31; petting zoo, gift shop, free noon tortoise feeding. ~30 min west. Approximate pin.

    8424 Bedell Rd, Berlin Center, OH

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB), Tripadvisor

  8. Worth the detour · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    TP Tools Auto Collection Museum

    A free classic-car museum inside the TP Tools complex — 50+ restored autos from 1917 on, staged amid immersive period sets: a 1950s diner, soda bar, country store and service garage.

    Your guide’s note Free; typically Saturdays 10–3, hours limited — confirm ahead. ~20 min south. Approximate pin.

    7075 State Route 446, Canfield, OH

    Recommended by Old Cars Weekly, Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB)

  9. Worth the detour · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Sports World Family Fun Center

    A long-running outdoor family fun center in Boardman — go-kart tracks, 18-hole adventure golf, batting cages and a redemption arcade — the valley's go-to for arcade-plus-outdoor play.

    Your guide’s note Seasonal outdoor attractions; pay-per-ride or packages. ~15 min south. Approximate pin.

    8249 South Ave, Boardman, OH

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB), Tripadvisor

  10. Worth the detour · Farms & U-Pick · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    White House Fruit Farm

    A big Canfield orchard and farm market open weekdays and weekends: orchard-fresh and pick-your-own apples, seasonal produce, and a fall gift barn famous for its apple-cider doughnuts and cider. The Valley's autumn tradition.

    Your guide’s note Open much of the year; busiest in fall. About 20 min out. Approximate pin.

    9249 Youngstown-Salem Rd, Canfield, OH

    Recommended by Explore Mahoning, WKBN 27 (local news)

  11. Worth the detour · Farms & U-Pick · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Detwiler Farm

    A family fall farm in Columbiana built for a day with kids: a hayride out to a 10-acre pick-your-own pumpkin patch, a straw maze and a 4-acre corn maze, plus a petting zoo and a tractor-tire playground.

    Your guide’s note Seasonal (fall), about $7 admission. ~30 min south. Approximate pin.

    4520 Renkenberger Rd, Columbiana, OH

    Recommended by WKBN 27 (local news), Northeast Ohio Family Fun

  12. Worth the detour · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Canfield Fairgrounds

    Home of the Canfield Fair, Ohio's largest county fair, over Labor Day week. The grounds are quiet off-season.

    Your guide’s note The fair is late Aug–Labor Day. Otherwise little to see. Seasonal.

    7265 Columbiana-Canfield Rd, Canfield, OH

    Recommended by Travel2Next

  13. Worth the detour · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Idora Park Experience

    The beloved Idora Park amusement park closed in 1984; volunteers now keep a museum of its memorabilia. A piece of vanished Youngstown, opened only on select days.

    Your guide’s note Limited hours — call or check ahead. The park itself is long gone. Approximate pin.

    4450 S Turner Rd, Canfield

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura

  14. Worth the detour · Markets · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Rogers Community Auction & Flea Market

    The largest open-air flea market in the tri-state area — over five miles of aisles and 1,000-plus vendor spaces of antiques, vintage, tools, produce and famous Amish doughnuts, going strong year-round. A proper day out for treasure hunters.

    Your guide’s note Fridays only, 7:30am to mid-afternoon, year-round. About 35–40 min south; wear walking shoes.

    45625 OH-154, Rogers, OH

    Recommended by Rogers Flea Market · Columbiana County

  15. Deep cut · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Hollywood Gaming at Mahoning Valley Race Course

    A racino (2014) pairing a one-mile thoroughbred track with 1,100+ video lottery terminals, dining and events — the region's live horse-racing venue.

    Your guide’s note Gaming areas 21+; live thoroughbred racing roughly Oct–April, free to watch. ~15 min northwest. Approximate pin.

    655 N Canfield-Niles Rd, Austintown, OH

    Recommended by WKBN 27, Explore Mahoning (Mahoning County CVB), Tripadvisor

  16. Deep cut · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Ernie Hall Aviation Museum

    A small but rich aviation museum honouring pioneer Ernest C. Hall — his 1947 Piper PA-12, personal letters between Hall and Orville Wright, and a scrap of fabric from the Red Baron's Fokker triplane.

    Your guide’s note Nonprofit, limited hours; hosts Wings-n-Wheels fly-ins. Confirm hours first. ~25 min north. Approximate pin.

    4033 North River Rd NE, Warren, OH

    Recommended by Ohio tourism, Tripadvisor

  17. Deep cut · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Ward-Thomas House Museum

    An 1862 fourteen-room Victorian mansion on the National Register, home to the Niles Historical Society's 5,000+ artefacts of local industrial heritage and reproductions of several First Ladies' inaugural gowns.

    Your guide’s note Very limited hours — typically the first Sunday of the month, 2–5, or by appointment. ~15 min north. Approximate pin.

    503 Brown St, Niles, OH

    Recommended by Niles Historical Society, Truly Trumbull (Trumbull County CVB)

  18. Deep cut · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Newton Falls Covered Bridge

    An 1831 covered bridge over the Mahoning River — the oldest covered bridge still in service in Ohio, with a rare attached covered pedestrian walkway.

    Your guide’s note Free, open to traffic and on foot year-round. ~25 min northwest. Approximate pin.

    Covered Bridge, Newton Falls, OH

    Recommended by Truly Trumbull (Trumbull County CVB)

  19. Deep cut · Drinks & Breweries · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Modern Methods Brewing Company

    Warren's first craft brewery since 1880, opened 2018 right on Dave Grohl Alley — IPAs, stouts and pilsners in a mural-wrapped tasting room.

    Your guide’s note In Warren, ~20 min north; pair with Dave Grohl Alley.

    125 David Grohl Alley, Warren, OH

    Recommended by Ohio Magazine

  20. Deep cut · Drinks & Breweries · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Birdfish Brewing Co.

    A community-minded small brewery in nearby Columbiana with a dozen rotating craft beers on tap — worth the drive south.

    Your guide’s note In Columbiana, ~25 min south. Check taproom hours. Approximate pin.

    140 E Park Ave, Columbiana, OH

    Recommended by Added by the guide (general knowledge)

  21. Deep cut · Farms & U-Pick · Mahoning Valley Day Trips

    Molnar Farms

    A popular Poland fall farm close to the city — a hayride to the pumpkin patch and a corn maze, cheap and cheerful.

    Your guide’s note Seasonal (fall), about $5 per person. ~15 min out. Approximate pin.

    3115 E Western Reserve Rd, Poland, OH

    Recommended by WKBN 27 (local news)

40 sights and 22 places to eat, drink & shop across the Mahoning Valley, each traceable to the source that named it.

How this guide was made

How the food list works

Youngstown's signature is Brier Hill pizza — a pepper-and-romano pie with little or no mozzarella. A cuisine tag needs a named dish, not a label. Anything tagged ADDED is from general knowledge and should be verified before a visit.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Sources were found and cross-checked with web search. Direct page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sourcing relied on search results, not full-page reads. The ranked sources for this city live in data/sources.json; the process is documented in docs/SOURCES.md.

YouTube & creators

Peter Santenello (4.2M) covered next-door East Palestine — regional, not the city itself; Phil Kidd walks downtown Youngstown; Explore Mahoning covers the Valley. The Google-Maps beta page carries the full creator panel.

Cleo beta — every place is carried from the current live guide, with its sources. Map tiles: © OpenStreetMap contributors; Esri. All destinations.
